case: SQLite STRICT ANY direct query result CSV round trip
previous_gap: SQLx represented an unrecognized declared ANY result type as NULL, so arbitrary query-result CSV did not activate the tagged storage-class encoding.
change: For result columns with SQLx table origins and unknown type metadata, the driver resolves declared type names from pragma_table_xinfo on the same connection. Ambiguous attached-schema origins are left unresolved; computed columns never inherit a source column type.
contract: Direct table-column results expose declared STRICT ANY metadata for ordinary, parameterized and transaction queries.
App CSV export uses the query result's recovered ANY metadata, then import restores INTEGER, REAL, TEXT, BLOB, empty TEXT and SQL NULL into a separate STRICT ANY table.
A computed expression does not inherit ANY metadata from its input column.
The metadata lookup is best-effort and does not change the decoded runtime value.
independent_oracle: Native SQLite typeof(value) and returned Value after importing the query-result CSV into a separate STRICT ANY table.

app_strict_any_contract.command: rtk proxy cargo test --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-app --lib sqlite_any_contract -- --test-threads=1

sqlite_driver.command: rtk proxy cargo test --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-driver-sqlite

clippy.command: rtk proxy cargo clippy --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-driver-sqlite --all-targets -- -D warnings

validation.format_and_diff_checks: cargo fmt --all -- --check and git diff --check passed

remaining: A zero-row SQLite result still has no column metadata in the current row-based result conversion.
Computed expressions and attached-schema origins remain untyped when SQLx cannot provide a declared type.
Other SQLite consumers, formats, storage-class/affinity combinations and installed GTK behavior remain open.
This case does not close B3 or qualify the 0.2.0 release.
